title: Traffic Ignite Control Index and Operator Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact operator-facing index for the first 72 hours of a traffic ignition (pilot -> wide ramp). Focus is on measurable thresholds and simple escalation steps so oncall, product ops, and incident commanders can coordinate quickly. Not a full runbook — think ‘control panel’ + quick heuristics.

Context and scope:
- Applies to hosted-api launches and Dedicated customer ramp tests where we control traffic targets.
- Primary owners: product-ops (lead), serving-runtime (secondary), sre for escalation.
- Intended usage: during initial traffic probes, slow-roll phases (1% -> 25% -> 100%), and post-rollout stabilization window.

High-level TL;DR checklist (operator cheatsheet):
1) Pre-ignite quick checks (T-minus 30 min):
   - Confirm schema and route config matches canary: route-id, model-version, rollout-weight.
   - Verify metrics pipeline is healthy: ingestion latency < 1m, no backlog in metrics-ingest-queue.
   - Ensure dedupe/caching warmers deployed for critical prefixes.
   - Slack channel #prod-ignite created and participants listed.

2) First probe (1% traffic):
   - Duration: 30m
   - KPIs to watch live: p50 token latency, p95 token latency, token-per-second (TPS), error-rate 5xx, reject-rate (quota/burst).
   - Immediate abort if: p95 latency increases > 2x baseline OR 5xx spike to > 0.5% sustained for 3 min OR model quality regression > threshold (see eval hash link).

3) Ramp steps and guardrails (1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%):
   - Minimum observation window per step: 30m (extend to 60m if any signal is yellow).
   - Criteria to advance: p95 latency <= baseline * 1.3 AND error-rate <= baseline + 0.2% AND no new high-severity alerts.
   - Soft-fallback: if p95 latency between 1.3x-1.8x but errors low, cap traffic and open performance-ticket for tuning.
   - Hard-abort: p95 latency > 1.8x OR error-rate > baseline + 1% -> rollback to previous weight immediately.

Operator KPIs and formulas (single-line for rapid parsing):
- Baseline p50 / p95: taken from last steady-state 24h before ignition. Label 'baseline_p50' and 'baseline_p95' in metrics dashboard.
- latency_delta_p95 = (current_p95 / baseline_p95)
- error_delta = current_5xx_pct - baseline_5xx_pct
- tokens_per_second_target = planned_qps * avg_tokens_per_request

Live signal priority order (what to fix first):
1) Errors (5xx / rejects)
2) Latency p95
3) Throughput (backpressure)
4) Model quality (if automated evals flag regression)

Quick escalation map (who to ping):
- Tier 0 (operator): product-ops oncall -> check metrics, confirm canary routing, throttle traffic.
- Tier 1: serving-runtime lead (Liam O'Connor) -> investigate kernel, batching, OOM, KV-cache issues.
- Tier 2: infra/SRE (Priya Singh) -> node health, autoscaling policies, network egress limits.
- Tier 3: model-owner / applied-ml (Diego Alvarez) -> quality regressions, prompt / tokenizer anomalies.

Recovery playbook (short):
- If errors spike: reduce canary weight to 0, enable fallback model variant, and trigger alert: JIRA-xxxxx (create).
- If latency increases but errors low: apply traffic cap to previous stable weight, increase batch size suggestions (if safe), toggle prefix cache TTL extension for common prompts.
- If autoscaler thrashes: pin instance group to recent steady size and request immediate SRE intervention to adjust cooldown windows.

Compact KPI tracker (3-column snapshot for standup):
- Step: 1% | elapsed: 12m | p95: 220ms (baseline 120ms) | delta: 1.83x (YELLOW) | errors: 0.03% (GREEN)
- Step: 5% | elapsed: - | p95: - | errors: -

Operator notes / heuristics:
- Prefer conservative advance if any downstream system (billing, observability) shows warning.
- Use the model-eval hash to decide if quality signals are actionable during ramp; false positives happen with short sample windows.
- When in doubt, keep canary weight at last-green state for 60-120 minutes and open asynchronous tickets for root cause analysis.

Open action items (owner + due):
- Add 'ignite' view to console models page (product-ops) — Maya Chen — due 2025-02-14.
- Create synthetic traffic job that mirrors 80th percentile tokens per call (sre) — Priya Singh — due 2025-01-20.
- Add automated p95 alert with 5-min suppression window (serving-runtime) — Liam O'Connor — due 2025-01-22.

Risks and mitigations log (short entries):
- Risk: sudden third-party auth token throttling increases latency. Mitigation: pre-warm auth tokens and add alternate auth route.
- Risk: customer-specific prompt causing KV cache blowup. Mitigation: enable per-customer prefix caps and monitor cache miss ratio.

Quick references and bookmarks:
- Metrics dashboard: /dashboards/ignite-control-index (use 'ignite' filter)
- Eval set: confluence:traffic-ignite-evals (quality threshold: mean BLEU drop < 1.5)
- Runbooks: infra/autoscaler-tuning; serving/runtime-fallbacks

Notes to self / TODOs (informal):
- Try adding a tiny synthetic-run after each step to validate model-output shape (not just latency).
- Explore adding an automated canary rollback classifier later (ML-driven) — sketch in /notebooks/canary-classifier.ipynb
- Coordinate with finance to track instantaneous cost burn at each step so commercial team can make early decisions on Dedicated ramps.

Revision history:
